title: Kubernetes operators: how a controller keeps a cluster in shape

slides.title: An operator is a controller that runs inside the cluster

children.text:
API server
Stores both and tells watchers what changed

Controller
Runs in a pod and watches the resource

Custom resource
Declares the state you want

slides.caveat: An operator manages only the resources it was written for.
slides.notes: Point at the cluster boundary first: everything here runs inside it.

slides.title: The controller closes the gap, again and again

children.text:
Desired state
The custom resource declares what should be running, and the controller reads it first.

Observe
The controller reads what is running now and compares it with the desired state.

Act
When the two differ, the controller changes the cluster, then observes again.

slides.caveat: Reconciliation repeats; it is not a one-time install step.
slides.notes: Walk the loop twice: once when the resource is created, once after someone deletes a pod by hand.

slides.title: Check: a managed pod is deleted. What happens?

children.text: A  Nothing until the operator is reinstalled
B  The controller notices and recreates it
C  The custom resource is deleted too

slides.notes: Answer: B. The controller observes the drift and acts to restore the desired state.
